subject: surgery
title: Oral Premalignant Lesions: Leukoplakia, Erythroplakia, and Oral Fibrosis

steps.tx: The World Health Organization defines **oral leukoplakia** as a predominantly white patch or plaque of the oral mucosa that cannot be wiped away and cannot be characterized clinically or pathologically as any other diagnosable disease. It is a diagnosis of exclusion primarily driven by chronic mucosal irritation from tobacco smoke, chewed smokeless tobacco, and alcohol abuse. Biopsy is mandatory to exclude invasive carcinoma and grade mucosal epithelial dysplasia.
steps.say: Oral leukoplakia is a persistent white patch on the oral mucosa that cannot be scraped off or attributed to another disease. It is strongly linked to tobacco use and requires biopsy to grade dysplasia.

rows: Homogeneous Leukoplakia
Uniform thin flat white plaque with shallow surface fissures
Low risk of malignancy ranging from one to five percent
Speckled (Erythroleukoplakia)
Mixed white and red mucosal plaques with irregular borders
High risk of malignant transformation between twenty and thirty percent
Nodular Leukoplakia
Raised firm granular or nodular white excrescences
Elevated malignant potential requiring multiple targeted incisional biopsies
Proliferative Verrucous
Widespread progressive multifocal exophytic hyperkeratosis
Extremely high malignant progression approaching seventy percent over time

steps.tx: This thick white plaque coats the lateral tongue and refuses to wipe away, the clinical behaviour that defines leukoplakia. The **lateral tongue** is a high-risk site, so a uniform surface should not breed complacency about malignant change. Biopsy grades the dysplasia hiding beneath the keratin and decides between surveillance, laser ablation and formal excision.
steps.say: A non-scrapable white plaque on the lateral tongue defines high-risk leukoplakia. Biopsy grades dysplasia before treatment is chosen.

vis.alt: Thick homogeneous white leukoplakia plaque on the lateral margin of the tongue that cannot be scraped off
vis.caption: Thick homogeneous white leukoplakia plaque on the lateral margin of the tongue. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: While leukoplakia presents as a white lesion, **oral erythroplakia** manifests as a fiery red, velvety plaque with well-defined margins that cannot be attributed to trauma or infection. Erythroplakia carries the highest malignant transformation potential of all oral mucosal disorders. Microscopic evaluation reveals severe epithelial dysplasia, carcinoma in situ, or invasive squamous cell carcinoma in more than eighty to ninety percent of all biopsied specimens, demanding prompt full-thickness excision.
steps.say: Oral erythroplakia appears as a bright red velvety patch and carries the highest risk of malignant transformation. Over eighty percent of cases harbor severe dysplasia or invasive cancer on histological evaluation.

left.title: Oral Leukoplakia
points: Overall malignant transformation rate is five percent
Incisional biopsy at most indurated or irregular sector

right.title: Oral Erythroplakia
points: Fiery red velvety patch with distinct margins
Epithelial atrophy with superficial dilated capillaries
Malignant transformation rate exceeds eighty percent
Requires immediate wide surgical excision with margins

steps.tx: Against the pink floor of mouth, this flat patch burns velvety red with a sharply defined edge. That is **erythroplakia**, uncommon beside leukoplakia yet far more dangerous, because most biopsies already show severe dysplasia, carcinoma in situ or invasive cancer. No red patch of this sort earns observation; it earns prompt full-thickness excision and histology.
steps.say: A velvety red floor-of-mouth patch indicates erythroplakia with very high malignant potential. Prompt excision and histology are mandatory.

vis.alt: Velvety fiery red erythroplakia patch on the floor of the mouth
vis.caption: Velvety fiery red erythroplakia patch on the floor of the mouth. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: In the Indian subcontinent, habitual chewing of betel quid and areca nut induces **oral submucous fibrosis**, a chronic progressive scarring disease of the oral cavity. Areca alkaloids, particularly arecoline, stimulate mucosal fibroblasts to produce excessive collagen while upregulating lysyl oxidase and downregulating endogenous collagenase. Patients develop severe burning sensation in the mouth when eating spicy food, widespread mucosal blanching, loss of elasticity, and progressive trismus that severely restricts mouth opening.
steps.say: Chewing areca nut drives oral submucous fibrosis, causing excessive collagen deposition and progressive trismus. Patients experience intense burning pain with spicy foods, mucosal blanching, and severe limitation of mouth opening.

steps.tx: Examination of a patient with advanced oral submucous fibrosis reveals dense, rigid fibrous bands running vertically through both buccal cheeks, surrounding the lips, and immobilizing the soft palate. The uvula often appears shrunken, pale, and bud-like. Because oral submucous fibrosis is a premalignant condition with a lifetime malignant transformation risk of three to eight percent, patients require lifelong surveillance, cessation of betel chewing, and **intralesional steroid injections** combined with hyaluronidase to alleviate severe trismus.
steps.say: Dense fibrous bands in the cheeks and palate restrict oral movement and shrink the uvula. Carrying up to an eight percent risk of malignancy, treatment involves habit cessation and intralesional steroid injections.

rows: Group I (Early)
Greater than thirty-five millimetres
Strict betel quid cessation, nutritional antioxidants, and jaw opening exercises
Group II (Moderate)
Twenty-five to thirty-five millimetres
Biweekly intralesional triamcinolone and hyaluronidase injections with physiotherapy
Group III (Severe)
Fifteen to twenty-five millimetres
Intralesional placental extract, pentoxifylline tablets, aggressive stretch therapy
Group IV (Advanced)
Less than fifteen millimetres
Surgical band excision, bilateral coronoidectomy, and buccal fat pad graft closure

steps.tx: Malignant transformation of high-risk mucosal lesions leads directly to **carcinoma of the tongue**, the most frequent intraoral squamous cell carcinoma. Over eighty-five percent arise on the lateral border of the oral tongue, within the anterior two-thirds anterior to the circumvallate papillae. Lesions typically present as a painless, indurated ulcer with rolled, everted margins or an infiltrating exophytic mass. Early perineural invasion along the lingual nerve causes referred otalgia to the ipsilateral ear.
steps.say: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue develops predominantly along the lateral border of the anterior two-thirds. It presents as an indurated, non-healing ulcer with referred ear pain mediated by the lingual nerve.

left.title: Oral Tongue Carcinoma
points: Anterior two-thirds anterior to circumvallate papillae
Somatic sensory innervation via lingual nerve (V3)
Strongly linked to tobacco and alcohol exposure
Lymphatic drainage to submandibular and upper deep cervical nodes

right.title: Base of Tongue Carcinoma
points: Sensory innervation via glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
Strongly associated with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)
Frequent early bilateral deep cervical lymph node metastases

steps.tx: Accurate staging of oral tongue malignancies requires precise histopathological assessment of the depth of invasion. Under the modern eighth edition American Joint Committee on Cancer system, every five millimetres of **depth of invasion** upstages the primary tumor category. For example, a superficial ulcer measuring one point five centimetres across but invading six millimetres into the intrinsic tongue musculature is classified as T2 rather than T1, reflecting its high risk of occult cervical lymphatic metastasis.
steps.say: Staging oral tongue cancer incorporates the depth of invasion measured in millimeters. An invasion depth exceeding five millimeters increases the tumor stage, correlating directly with occult cervical lymph node spread.

nodes.label: Indication for Elective Neck Dissection if DOI > 4mm

steps.tx: Because the intrinsic musculature of the tongue permits early submucosal tumor tracking across midline fascial planes, lesions of the ventral tongue and tip possess a high propensity for bilateral lymphatic metastasis. Primary lymphatic drainage from the oral tongue flows directly into level one submandibular lymph nodes and level two upper deep jugular nodes. Management of clinically node-negative necks with invasion greater than three to four millimetres mandates an **elective neck dissection** of levels one through three.
steps.say: Tongue cancers readily cross tissue planes, draining into levels one, two, and three cervical lymph nodes. Tumors invading beyond four millimeters warrant an elective supraomohyoid neck dissection.

rows: Level IA (Submental)
Between anterior bellies of digastric above hyoid bone
First echelon for cancer of anterior floor of mouth and tongue tip
Level IB (Submandibular)
Submandibular triangle between digastric and mandible
Primary echelon drainage for lateral border oral tongue carcinoma
Level IIA (Upper Jugular)
Skull base to hyoid, anterior to spinal accessory nerve
Most common site of regional lymph node metastasis in oral tongue SCC
Level III (Mid Jugular)
Hyoid bone superiorly to cricoid cartilage inferiorly
Routine component of supraomohyoid selective neck dissection

steps.tx: Definitive surgical therapy for oral tongue carcinoma entails a **wide local glossectomy** achieving at least one to one point five centimetres of three-dimensional clear surgical margins around all palpable induration. Depending on tumor volume, procedures range from partial glossectomy to hemiglossectomy or total glossectomy. Surgical defects of hemiglossectomy are reconstructed with vascularized radial forearm free flaps or anterolateral thigh flaps to restore tongue mobility, swallowing, and speech articulation.
steps.say: Surgical treatment requires wide glossectomy with one to one point five centimeters of clear surgical margins. Microvascular free flaps restore tongue volume and mobility to preserve speech and swallowing.

nodes.label: Radial Forearm or Anterolateral Thigh Flap
